facts: Human action recognition from well-segmented 3D skeleton data has been intensively studied.
Online action detection is more challenging.
Online action detection identifies the action type on the fly from the untrimmed stream.
Online action detection localizes the action positions on the fly from the untrimmed stream.
The paper studies the problem of online action detection from the streaming skeleton data.
The paper proposes a multi-task end-to-end Joint Classification-Regression Recurrent Neural Network.
The proposed network employs a joint classification and regression optimization objective.
The proposed network is capable of automatically localizing the start and end points of actions more accurately.
The proposed model leverages the merits of the deep Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) subnetwork.
The proposed model automatically captures the complex long-range temporal dynamics.
The proposed model naturally avoids the typical sliding window design.
The proposed model ensures high computational efficiency.
The subtask of regression optimization provides the ability to forecast the action prior to its occurrence.
The authors build a large streaming video dataset with annotations.
Experimental results on the authors' dataset and the public G3D dataset both demonstrate very promising performance of the authors' scheme.
entities: multi-task end-to-end Joint Classification-Regression Recurrent Neural Network
joint classification and regression optimization objective
deep Long Short-Term Memory ( LSTM ) subnetwork
